Danielle Ford

Nonpartisan candidate for Governor, Nevada · Challenger

Member of the Nevada State Board of Education (District 3); marketing strategist and public speaker

Danielle Ford is a member of the Nevada State Board of Education for District 3. She took office in January 2025 and previously served one term as a Clark County School District trustee. She is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for Governor of Nevada as a nonpartisan (No Political Party) candidate.

Where Ford stands

K-12 education funding
Proposes stricter review of education contracts and less reliance on out-of-state vendors for curriculum, textbooks, software and training. She says this could free up about $2 billion a year for teachers and classroom aides.
Education governance
Opposes out-of-state companies placing representatives on Nevada education boards or committees.
Standardized testing
Supports ending standardized testing and having teachers report students' progress directly to parents.
Data centers and energy costs
Opposes expanding data centers until Nevada adopts a statewide strategy for technology and artificial intelligence. She says Las Vegas does not need more data centers now.
Housing
Supports helping people move into existing homes by covering costs such as appliances and utility deposits. Opposes developments built only for rental use.
Two-party system
Argues that Nevada's two-party system is not working and says a vote for a nonpartisan candidate is not a wasted vote.

Background

  • Nevada State Board of Education, District 3, 2025–present (term ends 2029)
  • Clark County School District Board of Trustees, District F: won in 2018, served one term, lost reelection in 2022
  • Marketing strategist and public speaker (Danielle Ford Inc)
  • Endorsed by the Nevada State Education Association in the 2024 State Board of Education race
